trust_decision.summary: Whether enough bytes remain in an untrusted TPM2 state blob before reading; decided by the (UINT32)*size length checks in the basic unmarshal primitives, which wrongly pass once block_skip_read() has driven the signed remaining size negative by subtracting an unchecked attacker-chosen blocksize.

landing_point.why: The summary names block_skip_read() and its unchecked blocksize; this branch adds blocksize to the buffer pointer and subtracts it from *size with no bound against *size.

fix_sites.entry_point: TPMLIB_SetState (PERMANENT/VOLATILE) -> PERSISTENT_ALL_Unmarshal / VolatileState_Load; also startup NV load via the tpm_nvram_loaddata callback; also every TPM2 command parameter unmarshal

fix_sites.module_kind: low-level shared unmarshal primitive (Array_Unmarshal; the old signed comparison already rejected a negative size, so this change is cosmetic hardening)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/tpm2/Unmarshal.c:19-98 (shared primitives in a different file from the block-skip code in src/tpm2/NVMarshal.c:131-160, also used by TPM command parsing)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Weak: a solver who bounds blocksize in block_skip_read (NVMarshal.c:149-153) closes the reported trigger and can fairly say the primitives need no change, since the only other way to get a negative size is a state blob of 2 GiB or more.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Forward-compatible skipping: a block present in the stream but not needed by this build (future-version data, or algorithm blocks compiled out such as skip_alg_ecc/skip_alg_rsa) must still be skipped; a fix that rejects every has_block && !needs_block case breaks loading state written by newer libtpms or other build configs. The primitives also parse all TPM2 commands, so changing what they do at *size == 0 or for non-negative sizes breaks command parsing.

O6_input_shapes: negative remaining size reaching UINT8/BOOL reads (BOOL_Unmarshal -> UINT8_Unmarshal)
negative remaining size reaching UINT16 reads
negative remaining size reaching UINT32 reads
negative remaining size reaching UINT64 reads
negative remaining size reaching byte-array/TPM2B reads (Array_Unmarshal)

O7_producer.where: src/tpm2/NVMarshal.c:131-160 (block_skip_read produces the negative *size; the write side is block_skip_write_pop at src/tpm2/NVMarshal.c:108-120)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: VolatileState_Load uses the same unchecked (UINT32)*size cast before hashing *size - sizeof(hash) bytes; the published fix left it alone. It is reachable only when the initial INT32 size is negative, from a uint32 length cast to INT32.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A negative size here needs a state blob of 2 GiB or more (src/tpm_tpm2_interface.c:807, src/tpm2/StateMarshal.c:52), which callers never supply, and it does not involve block_skip_read.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A forward-skip of trailing newer-version bytes that advances *buffer by a stream-derived length without the existing *size > 0 guard.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already does the same skip-unknown-trailing-data job as block_skip_read, so a maintainer could easily have written it with only the unsigned compare.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A version-dependent array reader (ppList/auditCommands) that skips bytes past its truncation limit by moving the pointer directly instead of going through Array_Unmarshal.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code already truncates bigger arrays from later versions (line 4152); skipping the excess in place is a natural variant.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: String_Unmarshal-style length-prefixed reader without the *size < 0 term.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Line 315 shows the maintainer adds that term by hand; one sibling reader omitting it is plausible.

O9_family: memory safety: out-of-bounds read from signed/unsigned length confusion after an unchecked skip subtraction (CWE-125)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/ has TPM2 C tests (tests/tpm2_*.c, tests/nvram_offsets.c, tests/object_size.c) and a fuzzer (tests/fuzz.cc); none targets block_skip_read or a negative state size. A hidden test can call TPMLIB_SetState with a crafted blob.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Bound blocksize against *size in block_skip_read (NVMarshal.c:149-153) and leave the primitives' (UINT32)*size casts alone. This closes the reported trigger, so a behavioural test probably cannot tell it apart from the published fix.

out_of_scope_notes: The TPM2 marshal-side primitives in src/tpm2/TPMCmd/tpm/src/support/Marshal.c:51,71,92,115 use the same (UINT32)*size cast, but on the output direction with TPM-controlled sizes; not pursued.
src/tpm12 has its own state-loading code; not examined.
unverified: Whether CryptHashBlock at src/tpm2/Volatile.c:45 actually over-reads for a negative initial size depends on its length parameter type; not checked.
present_in_latest unknown because no latest release was provided.
O1 counts SetState, startup NV/volatile load callbacks and command parsing as entry points; reachability of a negative size from command parsing (the TPM2 command buffer size) was not checked.
